description:
## Goal

Write `test/filament/examples/todo_test.exs` — tests for the TodoList example from G1.

Two test groups:
1. **Rung 1** — plain ExUnit tests for `Todo.Store` (add, toggle, filter, isolation)
2. **Rung 2** — component isolation tests for `TodoList` and `TodoItem` using
   `Filament.Test.mount/3`, `click/2`, `submit/3`, `render_text/1`

This ticket establishes the test pattern followed by H2, H3, and H4. Read H1 before
starting H2 or H3.

## Deviation policy

Any deviation from this spec requires prior approval. Stop work, run
`bw comment <ticket-id> "..."` describing the conflict, reopen the ticket, and await
guidance. Do not improvise.

---

## 0. Prerequisites — read implementations first

Before writing any test code, read the following files to understand the exact API:

  - `examples/todo/lib/todo/store.ex` — Todo.Store API (add/2, toggle/2, filter/2, etc.)
  - `examples/todo/lib/todo_web/components/todo_list.ex` — TodoList props, render, events
  - `examples/todo/lib/todo_web/components/todo_item.ex` — TodoItem props and event handling
  - The Filament.Test module (wherever F1 placed it — check test/support/ or lib/filament/)
    for the exact signatures of mount/3, click/2, submit/3, render_text/1, has_class?/3

The G1 spec says TodoList uses `use_state(:filter, :all)` and `use_state(:new_text, "")`.
It reads from a `Todo.Store` on every render (imperative read in the render body).
Confirm this by reading the actual implementation. If the component has different props
or interaction patterns, adapt the tests to match what is actually built.

Also confirm how the TodoList passes a store to subcomponents. Check whether the store
pid is a prop, or looked up via a registered name. Tests must start a locally-named store
for isolation (no shared global state between tests).

---

## 1. Test file location

FILE: `test/filament/examples/todo_test.exs`

The `examples/todo/lib/` directory is already included in `filament/mix.exs`
`elixirc_paths(:test)` by G1, so `Todo.Store`, `TodoWeb.Components.TodoList`, and
`TodoWeb.Components.TodoItem` are all available in the test compile path without any
additional changes to `mix.exs`.

---

## 2. Rung-1 tests — Todo.Store domain

These are plain ExUnit tests with no Filament infrastructure. Each test starts its own
isolated `Todo.Store` with a unique name (no default module-level name — pass a pid or
registered name explicitly to avoid test interference).

```elixir
defmodule Filament.Examples.TodoTest do
  use ExUnit.Case, async: true
  import Filament.Test

  # ── Rung 1: domain ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  describe "Todo.Store" do
    setup do
      name = :"todo_store_#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"
      {:ok, pid} = Todo.Store.start_link(name: name)
      %{store: pid}
    end

    test "starts empty", %{store: store} do
      assert Todo.Store.all(store) == []
    end

    test "add/2 appends item with auto-incremented id", %{store: store} do
      :ok = Todo.Store.add(store, "Buy milk")
      :ok = Todo.Store.add(store, "Write tests")
      items = Todo.Store.all(store)
      assert length(items) == 2
      assert Enum.map(items, & &1.text) == ["Buy milk", "Write tests"]
      # IDs are unique integers, first item gets id=1
      assert Enum.map(items, & &1.id) == [1, 2]
    end

    test "toggle/2 flips the done flag", %{store: store} do
      :ok = Todo.Store.add(store, "Walk dog")
      [item] = Todo.Store.all(store)
      refute item.done

      :ok = Todo.Store.toggle(store, item.id)
      [toggled] = Todo.Store.all(store)
      assert toggled.done

      :ok = Todo.Store.toggle(store, item.id)
      [unset] = Todo.Store.all(store)
      refute unset.done
    end

    test "filter/2 returns :all, :active, :completed subsets", %{store: store} do
      :ok = Todo.Store.add(store, "active item")
      :ok = Todo.Store.add(store, "done item")
      [_a, d] = Todo.Store.all(store)
      :ok = Todo.Store.toggle(store, d.id)

      assert length(Todo.Store.filter(store, :all)) == 2
      active = Todo.Store.filter(store, :active)
      assert length(active) == 1
      assert hd(active).text == "active item"
      completed = Todo.Store.filter(store, :completed)
      assert length(completed) == 1
      assert hd(completed).text == "done item"
    end

    test "add/2 rejects empty string", %{store: store} do
      # Empty string should raise FunctionClauseError due to guard `text != ""`
      assert_raise FunctionClauseError, fn -> Todo.Store.add(store, "") end
      assert Todo.Store.all(store) == []
    end
  end
```

---

## 3. Rung-2 tests — TodoList component isolation

Use `Filament.Test.mount/3`, `click/2`, `submit/3`, `render_text/1`.
Start a local store per test; pass it as a prop to the component.

Read `examples/todo/lib/todo_web/components/todo_list.ex` to confirm:
- What prop(s) the component accepts (likely `:store`)
- The exact text content or HTML structure (what does the submit form look like? what
  does a todo item element look like? are there data-id or phx-value attributes?)
- How keyed rendering works (each `<.TodoItem>` should have a `:key` attribute)
- How filter buttons are rendered (what selectors can we use?)

Adapt selectors in the tests below to match the actual rendered HTML structure.

```elixir
  # ── Rung 2: component isolation ─────────────────────────────────────────────

  describe "TodoList component" do
    setup do
      name = :"todo_store_#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"
      {:ok, store} = Todo.Store.start_link(name: name)
      # Mount the component. Pass the store pid so each test has an isolated store.
      # If TodoList uses a registered name instead of a pid prop, adapt accordingly.
      {:ok, view} = mount(TodoWeb.Components.TodoList, %{store: store})
      %{store: store, view: view}
    end

    test "renders empty state on first mount", %{view: view} do
      # No items yet — confirm some indicator of an empty list.
      # Adapt this assertion to match what the component actually renders.
      html = view.rendered_html
      refute html =~ "<li"  # no list items
    end

    test "submit adds a new item and re-renders", %{view: view} do
      # Find the form and submit it with new todo text.
      # Check the actual phx-submit form selector in the component template.
      {:ok, view} = submit(view, "form", %{"text" => "Buy milk"})
      assert render_text(view) =~ "Buy milk"
    end

    test "clicking a todo item toggles its done state", %{view: view, store: store} do
      :ok = Todo.Store.add(store, "Write tests")

      # Re-mount or trigger a re-render so the new item appears.
      # Option A: re-mount fresh
      # Option B: click a filter button (which changes use_state and re-renders)
      # Read the implementation to determine which is needed. The simplest approach
      # is to mount with a store that already has items:
      {:ok, view2} = mount(TodoWeb.Components.TodoList, %{store: store})
      assert render_text(view2) =~ "Write tests"

      # Click the todo item to toggle it. Adapt the selector to the actual template.
      # The component likely renders a checkbox or button with phx-click per item.
      {:ok, toggled_view} = click(view2, "[data-todo-id]")
      html = toggled_view.rendered_html
      # After toggle, the item should be visually marked as done (e.g., class "done"
      # or strikethrough text). Adapt assertion to match actual rendered output.
      assert has_class?(toggled_view, "[data-todo-id]", "done") or
             html =~ "line-through" or
             html =~ "done"
    end

    test "filter buttons show correct subsets", %{view: view, store: store} do
      :ok = Todo.Store.add(store, "active item")
      :ok = Todo.Store.add(store, "done item")
      [_a, d] = Todo.Store.all(store)
      :ok = Todo.Store.toggle(store, d.id)

      # Mount fresh with items already in store
      {:ok, view} = mount(TodoWeb.Components.TodoList, %{store: store})

      # Click the "Active" filter button.
      # Adapt selector to match actual template (button text or data attribute).
      {:ok, filtered} = click(view, "button[phx-value-filter='active']")
      text = render_text(filtered)
      assert text =~ "active item"
      refute text =~ "done item"

      # Click the "Completed" filter button.
      {:ok, completed_view} = click(filtered, "button[phx-value-filter='completed']")
      text2 = render_text(completed_view)
      assert text2 =~ "done item"
      refute text2 =~ "active item"
    end

    test "keyed list re-render preserves identity across filter changes", %{store: store} do
      :ok = Todo.Store.add(store, "item-one")
      :ok = Todo.Store.add(store, "item-two")
      {:ok, view} = mount(TodoWeb.Components.TodoList, %{store: store})

      # Switch to active filter and back to all. Both items should still appear.
      # This validates that keyed rendering doesn't duplicate or drop items.
      {:ok, view} = click(view, "button[phx-value-filter='active']")
      {:ok, view} = click(view, "button[phx-value-filter='all']")
      text = render_text(view)
      assert text =~ "item-one"
      assert text =~ "item-two"
    end
  end
end
```

NOTE: The selectors above (`[data-todo-id]`, `button[phx-value-filter='active']`, etc.)
are educated guesses. Read the G1 implementation and adapt every selector to match the
actual rendered HTML. If the selectors differ significantly, use what is actually there —
do not add `data-*` attributes or change the component to match the tests.

---

## 4. Run tests

```
mix test test/filament/examples/todo_test.exs
```

---

## 5. Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `test/filament/examples/todo_test.exs` exists and compiles
- [ ] Rung-1 — all 5 `Todo.Store` tests pass (starts empty, add, toggle, filter, empty guard)
- [ ] Rung-2 — all 5 `TodoList` component tests pass (empty state, submit, toggle, filter,
      keyed re-render)
- [ ] Tests are isolated — no shared global state, each test starts its own store
- [ ] `async: true` is set (safe since no shared singletons)
- [ ] No changes to example source files — tests must adapt to the implementation, not
      the other way round. If an adaptation requires changing the component, stop and
      comment on this ticket.
- [ ] Full suite still passes: `mix test`
